title: Lanes fork from local main, and the carry trusts "on local main", not "on origin"
summary: laneStartRef (core/worktree.go, integrationHead) bases a new lane on the local main when main is ahead of origin. The fleet rebase targets local main, and the carry treats each commit on local main as a landed peer. In cycle 1830, peer lane 1829 rebased onto the stranded commit ba61c7341, and its push published that commit. A ship pushes the whole ancestry of its commit with no provenance check. The two-phase landing (ADR-0039 §8.1) stops ship from leaving main ahead of origin. A strand from an older binary, a dossier closeout and a manual commit can still put main ahead.
fix: A check for "landed" must ask origin. Base a lane on origin/main, or refuse a base whose commits origin does not hold and the journal does not prove. Make the carry and the fleet rebase treat only commits on origin as landed.
acceptance: A lane does not fork from a local main whose ahead commits are not journaled (red first)
The carry does not count an unpushed commit on local main as a landed peer (red first)
routed_reason: out of scope for the ship-landing lane (brief: secondary finding); core is a protected surface
